---
title: "read.table() takes apostrophes for quotes and # for a comment"
ref: DF-05
categories: [Data frames and lists]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "a table of 4 rows"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
lines <- "name;n
Mary D'Angelo;12
Martin;5
O'Neil;7
Smith;3"
people <- read.table(text = lines, sep = ";", header = TRUE)
people
nrow(people)

read.table(text = "ref;n\nA#3;12\nB;5", sep = ";", header = TRUE)
```
:::

## Why

By default, `read.table()` uses `quote = "\"'"`: the apostrophe opens a quoted string, which only closes at the next apostrophe, several lines further down. Everything in between becomes a single value. Here, three people are merged into one, and the table loses two rows without the slightest warning.

Likewise, `comment.char = "#"` cuts each line at the first `#`. A reference such as `A#3` truncates the line, and R stops on an error about the number of columns that does not point to the real culprit.

## The fix

State explicitly which quotes and which comments the file uses, or go through `read.csv()` and `read.csv2()`, which only accept double quotes and ignore `#`.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
read.table(text = lines, sep = ";", header = TRUE, quote = "\"", comment.char = "")
read.csv2(text = "ref;n\nA#3;12\nB;5")
```
:::
